1.x: Why most Peninsular rivers flow east
The **Western Ghats** are the main water divide; the Deccan Plateau is **higher in the west and slopes east** to the Bay of Bengal, so most large rivers flow **east**.

The Peninsular block was **tilted north-west → south-east** (Himalayan upheaval), giving the whole drainage a Bay of Bengal orientation – about **77%** of India's drainage area drains to the **Bay of Bengal** and about **23%** to the Arabian Sea.
**Narmada and Tapi** are the only major Peninsular rivers flowing **west** – they occupy **trough faults (rift valleys)**.

East-flowing Deccan rivers build deltas although the Deccan is hard rock: **Mahanadi** (delta near **Paradeep**, Odisha), Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri. The **Narmada, Tapi, Mandovi** end in **estuaries** (Narmada estuary ~27 km, south of **Bharuch**).

5.x: **Western Ghats** = "**Water Tower of Peninsular India**" – sources of the **Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri**.

**Amarkantak:** two major rivers rise here – the **Son** flows **north** to join the Ganga (Bay of Bengal) and the **Narmada** flows **west** to the Arabian Sea. **Radial drainage:** streams flow outward from a central height – **Amarkantak** (Narmada, Son, Mahanadi).

**Son – "actual" source:** usually given as **Amarkantak** (Sonmuda, ~1.5 km from Narmada Kund); the stricter view places its origin near **Pendra** – the village **Sonbachharwar**, Pendra tehsil (then **Bilaspur district**, now Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi, Chhattisgarh).
**Bhedaghat** (marble rocks, Jabalpur), Shahdol and Hoshangabad lie **on the course** of the Narmada, not at its source.
